label: Bonus Class 2
title: How English Counts the World
bigIdea: Every language draws its own map of the world: English decides that some things are counted (a coin, two coins) and some are measured (money, information), even when Arabic counts them; and English uses one 'you' where Arabic has five.
bigIdeaAr: كل لغة ترسم خريطتها الخاصة للعالم: الإنجليزية تقرّر أن بعض الأشياء تُعَدّ (a coin, two coins) وبعضها يُقاس (money, information) حتى لو كانت العربية تعدّها؛ وتستخدم الإنجليزية you واحدة حيث تستخدم العربية خمسة ضمائر.
builtOn: Lesson 5: Object pronouns (me, him, her, us, them, it)
Lesson 6: Possessive pronouns (mine, yours, his, hers)
Lesson 8: Countable and uncountable nouns, How much / How many

Vocabulary: message, contact, emoji, earbuds, jacket, notebook, wallet, sneakers, umbrella, lunchbox, snack, leftovers, groceries, fridge, ingredients, recipe, allowance, price tag, discount, receipt, budget, savings, cash, change, homework, schedule

objectives.en: I can explain the difference between countable and uncountable nouns and why it is a grammar choice, not a fact about the world.
objectives.ar: أستطيع أن أشرح الفرق بين الأسماء المعدودة وغير المعدودة، ولماذا هو اختيار نحوي وليس حقيقة عن العالم.

objectives.en: I can use information, advice, homework, furniture, news, money and luggage correctly (no -s, no 'a').
objectives.ar: أستطيع أن أستخدم information و advice و homework و furniture و news و money و luggage بشكل صحيح (بلا -s وبلا a).

objectives.en: I can count uncountable things with units: a piece of advice, a bottle of water.
objectives.ar: أستطيع أن أعدّ الأشياء غير المعدودة بوحدات: a piece of advice و a bottle of water.

objectives.en: I can translate Arabic أنتَ / أنتِ / أنتما / أنتم / أنتنّ into English and explain why English has only 'you'.
objectives.ar: أستطيع أن أترجم أنتَ/أنتِ/أنتما/أنتم/أنتنّ إلى الإنجليزية وأشرح لماذا ليس فيها إلا you.

keyTerms.meaning: A noun you can count: a coin, two coins. It has a plural and can take a / an.
A noun English treats as a mass: money, rice, information. No plural, no a / an.
A countable word that lets us count a mass: a piece of, a slice of, a bottle of.
An uncountable word for a whole group of different things: furniture (chairs, tables, beds...), luggage (bags, suitcases). Not the same as team or family, which are countable.
A grammar form for exactly two. Arabic has it (أنتما، هما، كتابان); modern English does not.
The person or people you talk to: you (Arabic أنتَ، أنتِ، أنتما، أنتم، أنتنّ).

linguisticsCorner.title: Languages cut the world into different pieces

facts.en: Countable or uncountable is a decision of the grammar, not of nature. Coins and money are the same thing in your wallet, but English counts coins and measures money.
facts.ar: كون الاسم معدوداً أو غير معدود قرار نحوي وليس من الطبيعة. العملات المعدنية والمال شيء واحد في محفظتك، لكن الإنجليزية تعدّ coins وتقيس money.

facts.en: Languages disagree: English says information (no plural), Arabic says معلومات and French says informations, both plural. English hair is uncountable, but French cheveux is plural.
facts.ar: اللغات تختلف: الإنجليزية تقول information (بلا جمع)، والعربية تقول معلومات، والفرنسية informations، وكلاهما جمع. و hair في الإنجليزية غير معدود، لكنه جمع في الفرنسية (cheveux).

facts.en: English often uses a general 'mass' word for a group of different things: furniture (chairs, tables, beds), luggage (bags, suitcases), homework (exercises, tasks). Arabic أثاث is also one word for the whole group (one item is قطعة أثاث), but Arabic easily makes plurals such as واجبات, and in modern use you also hear أثاثات.
facts.ar: كثيراً ما تستخدم الإنجليزية كلمة «كتلة» عامة لمجموعة أشياء مختلفة: furniture للكراسي والطاولات والأسرّة، و luggage للحقائب، و homework للتمارين. وكلمة «أثاث» في العربية تدلّ أيضاً على المجموعة كلها (والقطعة الواحدة «قطعة أثاث»)، لكن العربية تجمع بسهولة مثل «واجبات»، وفي الاستعمال الحديث نسمع أيضاً «أثاثات».

facts.en: Some English nouns change meaning when they cross the line: chicken (meat) / a chicken (the animal); paper (material) / a paper (a newspaper); a coffee in a café means a cup of coffee.
facts.ar: بعض الأسماء الإنجليزية يتغيّر معناها حين تعبر الحدّ: chicken (لحم) و a chicken (الحيوان)، و paper (مادة الورق) و a paper (صحيفة)، و a coffee في المقهى تعني فنجان قهوة.

facts.en: English once had thou for one person and ye/you for more than one (ye was the subject form, you the object form). Like French vous, ye/you also became the polite way to speak to one person. Over time you replaced both ye and thou; thou now lives only in old prayers, poems and a few northern English dialects.
facts.ar: كان في الإنجليزية قديماً thou لشخص واحد و ye/you لأكثر من شخص (ye للفاعل و you للمفعول). وكما في الفرنسية vous صارت ye/you أيضاً صيغة الاحترام لمخاطبة شخص واحد. ومع الوقت حلّت you محل ye و thou معاً، ولم تبقَ thou إلا في الصلوات والأشعار القديمة وبعض لهجات شمال إنجلترا.

facts.en: Speakers still want a plural 'you', so they invent one: 'you guys' (US), 'y'all' (southern US), 'youse' (Ireland, Australia). Language keeps fixing its own gaps!
facts.ar: ما زال المتحدثون يحتاجون you للجمع فيخترعونها: you guys في أمريكا، و y'all في جنوب أمريكا، و youse في أيرلندا وأستراليا. اللغة تسدّ ثغراتها بنفسها!

arabicBridge.point: These are plural in Arabic, so learners add -s: informations, advices, homeworks, newses. In English they stay singular: much information, some advice.
arabicBridge.pointAr: هذه الكلمات جمع في العربية، فيضيف المتعلم -s: informations و advices. أما في الإنجليزية فتبقى مفردة: much information و some advice.

arabicBridge.english: a piece of advice / a piece of information / a piece of furniture
arabicBridge.point: Arabic makes a singular directly (نصيحة، معلومة). English needs a unit word to count a mass: a piece of.
arabicBridge.pointAr: العربية تصوغ المفرد مباشرة (نصيحة، معلومة)، أما الإنجليزية فتحتاج كلمة وحدة لتعدّ الكتلة: a piece of.

arabicBridge.point: News ends in -s but it is uncountable and singular: The news is good. Money is singular too: Money is important (not 'Moneys are').
arabicBridge.pointAr: news تنتهي بـ -s لكنها غير معدودة ومفردة: The news is good. و money مفردة أيضاً: Money is important.

arabicBridge.english: you (one word for 1, 2 or 100 people, boys or girls)
arabicBridge.point: Arabic shows gender and number (singular, dual, plural) in 'you'; English shows neither. Context tells you who is meant. The verb never changes either: you play, for everyone.
arabicBridge.pointAr: العربية تُظهر الجنس والعدد (مفرد ومثنى وجمع) في ضمير المخاطب، والإنجليزية لا تُظهر أياً منهما، والسياق يوضّح المقصود. والفعل لا يتغيّر أيضاً: you play للجميع.

arabicBridge.point: English keeps gender only in he/she (and him, his, her, hers). They covers two people and more, boys or girls.
arabicBridge.pointAr: الإنجليزية تحتفظ بالتذكير والتأنيث في he/she فقط (و him و his و her و hers). أما they فتشمل اثنين فأكثر، ذكوراً أو إناثاً.

arabicBridge.english: his / her follows the owner, like Arabic
arabicBridge.point: Same logic in both languages: his bag = the bag of a boy, her bag = the bag of a girl. The bag itself has no gender in English.
arabicBridge.pointAr: المنطق واحد في اللغتين: his bag حقيبة ولد، her bag حقيبة بنت. والحقيبة نفسها لا جنس لها في الإنجليزية.

commonErrors.why: Arabic معلومات is plural, so learners add -s. In English information is uncountable.

commonErrors.wrong: She gave me an advice. / two advices
commonErrors.right: She gave me some advice. / a piece of advice / two pieces of advice
commonErrors.why: Arabic has نصيحة / نصائح. English advice has no singular with a and no plural.

commonErrors.right: I have a lot of homework. / I have many homework tasks.
commonErrors.why: Arabic واجبات is plural. English homework is uncountable; count the tasks or exercises instead.
Furniture is an uncountable group word; to count, say pieces of furniture or name the items (two chairs).
News looks plural but is uncountable and takes a singular verb.

commonErrors.wrong: How many money do you have?
commonErrors.right: How much money do you have?
commonErrors.why: Money is uncountable: how much. Coins and dirhams are countable: how many coins.

commonErrors.right: My luggage is heavy. / My bags are heavy.
commonErrors.why: Luggage is uncountable in English, even though it means several bags.

commonErrors.wrong: This is mine pen. / Is this pen your?
commonErrors.right: This is my pen. / Is this pen yours?
commonErrors.why: Arabic uses the same ending for both (قلمي، القلم لي). English has two forms: my/your before a noun, mine/yours alone.

commonErrors.right: Are you ready? / Are you both ready? / Are you guys ready? (informal)
commonErrors.why: Yous/youse is used in some dialects (for example in Ireland and Australia), but standard English has no plural form of you; add both, all or guys (informal) to show number, as Arabic shows it with أنتما / أنتم.

teacher: Slide: Hamad's shopping bag with 12 items (coins, cash, rice, eggs, snacks, juice, receipt, bread, earbuds, money, ingredients, water)
Slide: two big boxes 'COUNT IT' (a, an, many, numbers) and 'MEASURE IT' (much, a piece of, a bottle of)
Slide: the You Map (أنتَ، أنتِ، أنتما، أنتم، أنتنّ → you)
Quiz-show scoreboard (Team Noor vs Team Ziad)
Picnic budget card: 50 dirhams, price list
student: Two cards: C (countable) and U (uncountable), made at the start of class

stages.name: Warm-up: Hamad's Shopping Bag
stages.method: Noticing challenge (can you put a number in front of it?)
stages.purpose: Activate Lesson 7-8 words and show a puzzle: some things take numbers and some don't, even when they look similar.
teacherSays: Hamad went shopping with his allowance. Here's his bag! Look at the 12 things.
Challenge: put a number in front of each one. Three eggs? Fine. Three rice? Hmm. Three moneys? Strange!
Which ones sound strange with a number? Write them in the chat. 60 seconds!
teacherSaysAr: ضعوا رقماً قبل كل كلمة. أي الكلمات تبدو غريبة مع رقم؟
studentsDo: Try 'two ___' with each item and type the strange ones in the chat.
Make the C and U cards.
tips: Expect a debate on money vs coins: perfect, that is today's mystery.
Do not explain yet; let the confusion build curiosity.

stages.name: Discovery: Count It or Measure It?
stages.method: Guided discovery + sorting with response cards
stages.purpose: Students find the grammar signals of countable and uncountable nouns: a/an, plural -s, many vs much, few vs little.
teacherSays: Look at these two lists. List 1: a coin, two coins, many coins. List 2: money, some money, a lot of money. What can list 1 do that list 2 can't?
Yes! Countable nouns take a or an, a plural -s and many. Uncountable nouns take none of these. They use much, some, a lot of.
Uncountable things are often liquids (water, juice), tiny grains (rice, sugar), materials (paper, glass), ideas (advice, information) or group words (money, furniture).
Now show me C or U for each word. Ready? Three, two, one, show!
teacherSaysAr: الاسم المعدود يأخذ a/an وجمع -s و many. وغير المعدود لا يأخذها، بل يأخذ much و some و a lot of.
غالباً ما يكون غير المعدود سائلاً، أو حبوباً صغيرة، أو مادة، أو فكرة، أو كلمة تجمع أشياء كثيرة.
studentsDo: Complete the rule table on the slide (a/an? plural? many or much?).
Show C or U for each word.
Give a reason for 2 tricky ones (e.g. why groceries and leftovers are always plural).

items.answer: C (usually plural: a pair of earbuds)

tips: Groceries and leftovers are plural-only words (like scissors): 'The groceries are in the fridge.' Mention it as a bonus fact.
'Change' = coins you get back is uncountable; 'a change' = something different is countable. Great example of a meaning switch.

stages.name: Linguistics Corner: Every Language Draws Its Own Map
stages.nameAr: ركن اللغويات: كل لغة ترسم خريطتها
stages.purpose: Understand that countability is a grammar choice that varies across languages, and learn the 'unit trick' to count any mass.
teacherSays: Here's a big idea from linguistics: languages cut the world into different pieces.
In your wallet you have coins. English counts them. But put them together and call them money, and English stops counting. Same thing, different grammar!
Arabic says معلومات, plural. French says informations, plural. English says information, never plural. Who's right? Everybody! Each language has its own map.
So how does English count a mass? With a unit: a bottle of water, a slice of bread, a piece of advice. The unit is countable: two bottles of water.
Funny ones: chicken is meat, a chicken is an animal! Paper is the material, a paper is a newspaper.
teacherSaysAr: اللغات تقطّع العالم قطعاً مختلفة، ولا توجد لغة «صحيحة» وأخرى «خاطئة».
لعدّ شيء غير معدود نستخدم وحدة: a bottle of water و a piece of advice.
studentsDo: Match each mass noun to its unit.
Say a full phrase with a number: 'two slices of bread'.
Discuss: 'Name one thing Arabic counts and English doesn't.'

exercise.instructions: Match the uncountable noun to a unit. Then say it with the number 2.
exercise.instructionsAr: صِل الاسم غير المعدود بوحدته، ثم قلها مع الرقم 2.

items.answer: a bottle of water → two bottles of water
a slice / loaf of bread → two slices of bread
a piece of advice → two pieces of advice
a piece of information → two pieces of information
a piece of furniture → two pieces of furniture
a bag / bowl of rice → two bags of rice
a glass / carton of juice → two glasses of juice
a piece of news → two pieces of news
a piece of luggage → two pieces of luggage (or: two bags)

tips: Accept any sensible unit (a bowl of rice, a cup of juice).
Keep the French example short; the point is that Arabic is not 'wrong', just different.

stages.name: Arabic Bridge: The 'Informations' Trap
stages.purpose: Target the exact words that are plural in Arabic but uncountable in English, and fix the errors they cause.
teacherSays: Here are the trap words. In Arabic most of them are plural: معلومات، نصائح، واجبات، أخبار، أمتعة، فلوس, and أثاث is easy to count as قطع أثاث. In English: information, advice, homework, furniture, news, luggage, money. No -s, no a, singular verb!
Your brain translates from Arabic and adds an -s. That's normal: it's called transfer. Now we train the brain to stop.
Two tricks: 1) use some, a lot of, much. 2) count with a piece of, or count the real things: two homework tasks, three bags.
Race time! Fix the sentences. First correct answer in the chat wins.
teacherSaysAr: أغلب هذه الكلمات جمع في العربية، لكنها غير معدودة في الإنجليزية: لا -s ولا a، والفعل مفرد.
يسمّي اللغويون هذا «النقل من اللغة الأم»، وهو طبيعي. لنتدرّب على تجنّبه.
studentsDo: Read the Arabic/English pairs aloud.
Race: correct each sentence in the chat.
Write one true sentence with one trap word about their own life.

exercise.instructions: Each sentence has one mistake. Fix it fast!
exercise.instructionsAr: في كل جملة خطأ واحد. صحّحه بسرعة!

items.prompt: Noor has a lot of homeworks tonight.
items.answer: Noor has a lot of homework tonight.

items.prompt: Can you give me an advice about my budget?
items.answer: Can you give me some advice / a piece of advice about my budget?

items.prompt: The price tag has some useful informations.
items.answer: The price tag has some useful information.

items.prompt: The news are on TV at eight.
items.answer: The news is on TV at eight.

items.prompt: How many money is in your wallet?
items.answer: How much money is in your wallet?

items.prompt: Our new furnitures are from a sale.
items.answer: Our new furniture is from a sale.

items.prompt: I have two advices for you.
items.answer: I have two pieces of advice for you.

items.prompt: Sara saves her moneys in a moneybox.
items.answer: Sara saves her money in a moneybox.

tips: Say 'transfer is normal' with warmth: teens are relieved that the mistake has a reason.
Note for the teacher: 'moneys / monies' exists in legal English, but students should never use it.

stages.name: The 'You' Puzzle: One Word for Five
stages.method: Contrastive pronoun map + history story + translation challenge
stages.purpose: Show how Arabic pronouns mark gender and number (including dual) while English 'you' marks neither, and practice translating with context words (both, all, guys).
teacherSays: Arabic, how many words for 'you'? Let's count: أنتَ، أنتِ، أنتما، أنتم، أنتنّ. Five! Boy or girl, one, two or many.
English? One: you. You, Omar. You, Sara. You two. You, the whole class. Always you!
Did English always have one? No! 600 years ago it had thou for one person and ye or you for more. You also became the polite word, like a sign of respect, and thou slowly disappeared.
Then people missed a plural, so they invented new ones: you guys, y'all. Language fixes its own holes!
So how do we show 'two' in English? We add a word: you both, you two, both of you. And 'all of you' for a group.
Third person: هو، هي → he, she. But هما، هم، هنّ → all become they. English keeps gender only in he and she and their other forms: him, his, her, hers.
teacherSaysAr: في العربية خمسة ضمائر للمخاطب، وفي الإنجليزية ضمير واحد: you.
كانت thou قديماً للمفرد و ye/you للجمع، ثم صارت you للجميع.
لإظهار العدد نضيف كلمة: you both أو all of you. وهما وهم وهنّ كلها تصبح they.
studentsDo: Translate the Arabic sentences into English, adding both/all when it helps.
Answer: 'Which language gives more information in its pronouns? Which is simpler to learn?'
Write one sentence using an object pronoun (them, her) and one possessive (hers, theirs) from Lessons 5-6.

exercise.instructions: Translate into English. Keep the meaning of number (one, two, many) when needed.
exercise.instructionsAr: ترجم إلى الإنجليزية، وحافظ على معنى العدد (واحد، اثنان، جمع) عند الحاجة.

items.answer: You are my friends. / You two are my friends. / You are both my friends.
Are you ready? / Are you all ready?
They send a message. / They are sending a message.
You (all) save money for the trip. / You are all saving money for the trip.
Is this wallet yours or hers?

tips: Avoid saying English is 'poorer': it shows the same information with other words (both, all) or context.
If students ask about 'they' for one unknown person ('Someone left their jacket'): yes, English uses it, and has done for centuries.

stages.name: Team Quiz Show: How Much or How Many?
stages.nameAr: مسابقة الفرق: How much أم How many؟
stages.method: Gamified retrieval practice (quiz show with point values)
stages.purpose: Practice the full system fast: a/an vs some, some vs any, much vs many, units, singular verb with uncountable nouns.
teacherSays: Welcome to 'Count Me In!', the quiz show. Team Noor against Team Ziad!
Easy questions are 1 point, hard ones are 3 points. Choose your level!
Discuss for 15 seconds, then one team captain answers. If you're wrong, the other team can steal the points.
teacherSaysAr: أهلاً بكم في مسابقة Count Me In! الأسئلة السهلة بنقطة، والصعبة بثلاث نقاط.
إن أخطأ فريق يستطيع الفريق الآخر سرقة النقاط.
studentsDo: Choose a question level, discuss quickly, and answer.
Explain each answer with the rule (C or U?).
Steal points by correcting the other team.

exercise.instructions: Complete the sentence. Say why (countable or uncountable?).
exercise.instructionsAr: أكمل الجملة واذكر السبب (معدود أم غير معدود؟).

items.prompt: How ___ snacks are in the pantry? (1 pt)
How ___ cash do you have? (1 pt)
Is there ___ milk in the fridge? (1 pt)
I'd like ___ apple and ___ bread. (2 pts)
We don't have ___ ingredients for the recipe. (2 pts)
There ___ (is / are) a lot of information on the receipt. (2 pts)
How ___ homework do you get on weekdays? (2 pts)
Can I give you ___ advice? It's about your savings. (3 pts)
Ask about price: 'How much ___ these sneakers?' (3 pts)
Correct it: 'The leftovers is in the fridge.' (3 pts)
items.answer: The leftovers are in the fridge. (leftovers is plural-only)

tips: Online: captains type answers in the chat after a 15-second countdown, so the other team can't copy.
Item 9 is a classic: 'How much' asks about price with any noun, because we're really asking about money.

stages.name: Production: The Crew Picnic Budget
stages.method: Task-based role-play (planning with a budget and a price list)
stages.purpose: Use countable/uncountable nouns, some/any, how much/many and pronouns in a realistic planning conversation.
teacherSays: The crew is planning a picnic. Your budget is 50 dirhams. Look at the price list: water 1 dirham a bottle, juice 2 dirhams a bottle, bread 3 dirhams a loaf, snacks 1 dirham each, rice 4 dirhams a bag, fruit 5 dirhams a box.
In pairs, plan your shopping list. Ask: How many bottles of juice do we need? How much rice? Do we have any leftovers in the fridge?
Then present: 'We need four bottles of water, three bottles of juice and two loaves of bread. We don't need any rice. That's 16 dirhams, so we have 34 dirhams left.'
teacherSaysAr: عندكم 50 درهماً لنزهة الفريق. خطّطوا قائمة التسوق بالأسئلة: How many و How much و any.
studentsDo: Plan a shopping list in pairs using at least 6 items, 2 units and 4 questions.
Present the plan in 4-5 sentences.
Listeners check: is the budget correct? Is every noun right (C or U)?
tips: Write the useful frames on screen: How many ___ do we need? / How much ___ is there? / We need some ___. / We don't need any ___.
If time is short, let one pair present and the other give feedback.

stages.name: Exit Ticket and Did You Know?
stages.purpose: Check each student alone on the trap words and the 'you' contrast.
teacherSays: Exit ticket: five items, privately in the chat to me.

Did you know? Fish is usually the same in the plural (one fish, ten fish), and 'fishes' is used mainly for different kinds of fish. And in Arabic, سمك is a collective word and سمكة is one fish. Languages love playing with counting!
Mission: teach someone at home the 'informations' trap.
teacherSaysAr: هل تعلم؟ في العربية «سمك» اسم جنس جمعي و«سمكة» للواحدة، والإنجليزية أيضاً تلعب بالعدّ بطرق عجيبة.
مهمتك: علّم أحداً في البيت فخ «informations».
studentsDo: Answer 5 items privately.
Share one 'map' difference between English and Arabic.
tips: Note who still writes informations/advices; recycle in Lessons 9-12 (Lesson 12 uses advice a lot!).

items.prompt: Correct: 'I need some informations about the sale.'
items.answer: I need some information about the sale.

items.prompt: How ___ (much / many) receipts are in your wallet?

items.answer: You are (both) ready. / You two are ready.

homework.en: Kitchen and Wallet Detective: list 10 things in your kitchen or your bag, write C or U next to each, and write 6 sentences using some, any, how much, how many and a piece of / a bottle of. Then write 3 sentences that use the trap words correctly (homework, advice, information).
homework.ar: محقق المطبخ والمحفظة: اكتب 10 أشياء في مطبخك أو حقيبتك، وضع C أو U بجانب كل منها، واكتب 6 جمل باستخدام some و any و how much و how many و a piece of / a bottle of. ثم اكتب 3 جمل تستخدم فيها كلمات الفخ بشكل صحيح (homework و advice و information).
tasks: List and label 10 nouns (C or U).
Write 6 sentences with some / any / how much / how many / units.
Write 3 correct sentences with homework, advice and information.
Bonus: ask a family member how many words for 'you' they know in other languages.

support: Keep the C/U lists on screen during all games.
Give only the 4 most common trap words first (information, advice, homework, money).
In translation, give the English pronoun options (you / they / she / him / hers) as a word bank.
challenge: Find 3 words that can be both C and U with different meanings (chicken, paper, coffee, time: 'I have no time' / 'three times').
Explain why we say 'a few coins' but 'a little money'.
Investigate 'they' for one person: find an example in a book or a website.

successCriteria: Labels at least 10 of 12 nouns correctly as C or U.
Uses the 7 trap words without -s and without a in writing and speech.
Uses at least two unit phrases correctly (a piece of, a bottle of).
Translates Arabic second-person pronouns into English and adds both / all when needed.
Explains in a sentence that countability is a grammar choice that differs between languages.
watchFor: an advice / a homework / a news
Adding a plural marker to you ('yous') or confusing he/she in fast speech

teacherNotes: This class explains Lessons 5-8; it uses their vocabulary (money words from Lesson 8, food from Lesson 7, belongings from Lesson 6).
Advice, information, furniture, news and luggage are named in the outline because they are the classic trap words for Arabic speakers; advice returns in Lesson 12, so this class pre-teaches the trap.
Present Arabic as a valuable tool: 'You already know the idea of a unit: سمكة from سمك, نصيحة as one advice.'
Bonus Class 3 moves from 'grammar maps' to 'word building': how English and Arabic make new words.

deck.title: Put a number in front of each thing
deck.text: Three eggs? Fine. Three rice? Hmm. Three moneys? Strange! Which ones sound strange with a number?
deck.ar: ضع رقماً قبل كل كلمة. أي الكلمات تبدو غريبة مع رقم؟

deck.title: What can list 1 do that list 2 can't?
rows: things you count one by one
deck.note: Uncountable: water, rice, paper, advice, information, money, furniture.
deck.noteAr: غير المعدود غالباً سائل أو حبوب أو مادة أو فكرة أو كلمة تجمع أشياء كثيرة.

deck.title: Same thing, different grammar
deck.text: Who's right? Everybody! Each language draws its own map of the world.
deck.ar: اللغات تقطّع العالم قطعاً مختلفة، ولا توجد لغة «صحيحة» وأخرى «خاطئة».

deck.title: Count a mass with a unit

cards.head: a bottle of
cards.sub: water, juice → two bottles of water

deck.instructions: Match the uncountable noun to a unit. Then say it with the number 2.
deck.instructionsAr: صِل الاسم غير المعدود بوحدته، ثم قلها مع الرقم 2.

deck.title: Cross the line, change the meaning
bullets: coffee · a coffee in a café (= a cup of coffee)
change (coins you get back) · a change (something new)
deck.ar: بعض الأسماء يتغيّر معناها حين تصبح معدودة.

deck.title: Plural in Arabic, uncountable in English
deck.note: Your brain adds -s from Arabic. That's transfer, and it's normal! No -s, no a, singular verb.
deck.noteAr: يسمّي اللغويون هذا «النقل من اللغة الأم»، وهو طبيعي: لا -s ولا a، والفعل مفرد.

deck.instructions: Each sentence has one mistake. Fix it fast!
deck.instructionsAr: في كل جملة خطأ واحد. صحّحه بسرعة!

items.prompt: Noor has a lot of homeworks tonight.
Can you give me an advice about my budget?
items.answer: some advice / a piece of advice

items.prompt: The price tag has some useful informations.
The news are on TV at eight.
How many money is in your wallet?
Our new furnitures are from a sale.
I have two advices for you.
Sara saves her moneys in a moneybox.

deck.title: Five Arabic words, one English word
deck.note: To show number, add a word: you two, you both, all of you.
deck.noteAr: لإظهار العدد نضيف كلمة: you two أو you both أو all of you.

deck.title: How English lost its plural 'you'

steps.label: Long ago · ye / you
steps.sub: for more people, then the polite word for one

steps.label: Later · you
steps.sub: you replaced both ye and thou
steps.ar: حلّت you محل ye و thou

deck.note: Thou lives on only in old prayers, poems and a few northern English dialects.
deck.noteAr: لم تبقَ thou إلا في الصلوات والأشعار القديمة وبعض لهجات شمال إنجلترا.

deck.title: Third person: Arabic and English
deck.note: English keeps gender only in he and she (him, his, her, hers). They = two or more.
deck.noteAr: الإنجليزية تحتفظ بالتذكير والتأنيث في he و she فقط، و they لاثنين فأكثر.

deck.instructions: Translate into English. Keep the meaning of number (one, two, many) when needed.
deck.instructionsAr: ترجم إلى الإنجليزية، وحافظ على معنى العدد (واحد، اثنان، جمع) عند الحاجة.

items.answer: They send / are sending a message.
You (all) save money for the trip.
Is this wallet yours or hers?

deck.instructions: Complete the sentence. Say why (countable or uncountable?).
deck.instructionsAr: أكمل الجملة واذكر السبب (معدود أم غير معدود؟).

items.prompt: How ___ snacks are in the pantry? (1 pt)
How ___ cash do you have? (1 pt)
Is there ___ milk in the fridge? (1 pt)
I'd like ___ apple and ___ bread. (2 pts)
We don't have ___ ingredients for the recipe. (2 pts)
There ___ (is / are) a lot of information. (2 pts)
How ___ homework do you get on weekdays? (2 pts)
Can I give you ___ advice? It's about your savings. (3 pts)
Ask about price: 'How much ___ these sneakers?' (3 pts)
Correct it: 'The leftovers is in the fridge.' (3 pts)
items.answer: The leftovers are in the fridge.

deck.title: Your budget: 50 dirhams
deck.note: How many bottles of juice do we need? · How much rice? · Do we have any leftovers?
deck.noteAr: خطّطوا قائمة التسوق: How many و How much و any.

deck.title: Plan, then present
steps: In pairs, plan a list: at least 6 items and 2 units.
Ask 4 questions: How many ___ do we need? How much ___ is there?
Use: We need some ___. / We don't need any ___.
Present: 'We need four bottles of water... That's 16 dirhams.'
Listeners: check the budget and every noun (C or U).
deck.ar: خطّطوا في أزواج ثم قدّموا خطتكم، والمستمعون يتحققون من الميزانية ومن كل اسم.

deck.ribbon: Did you know · one fish, ten fish
deck.text: Fish is usually the same in the plural: one fish, ten fish. 'Fishes' is used mainly for different kinds of fish. In Arabic, سمك is a collective word and سمكة is one fish.
deck.ar: في العربية «سمك» اسم جنس جمعي و«سمكة» للواحدة، والإنجليزية أيضاً تلعب بالعدّ.

homeworkMissions.intro: Five missions about counting the world in English. Finish them all to earn your Count Master badge!
homeworkMissions.introAr: خمس مهمات عن العدّ في الإنجليزية. أنجزها كلها لتحصل على شارة سيّد العدّ!

missions.title: How Much or How Many?
missions.intro: Listen to the word. Do you ask How much or How many?
missions.introAr: استمع إلى الكلمة: هل تسأل How much أم How many؟

missions.title: Count It or Measure It?
missions.intro: Tap a word, then tap its box.

items.qAr: كلمة information ليس لها جمع في الإنجليزية.
جملة The news are bad صحيحة.
items.why: News is uncountable and singular: The news is bad.

items.q: We can say 'a piece of advice'.
items.qAr: نستطيع أن نقول a piece of advice.

items.q: Arabic معلومات is plural, but English information is uncountable.
items.qAr: كلمة «معلومات» جمع في العربية، لكن information غير معدودة في الإنجليزية.

items.q: English has a special 'you' for two people, like Arabic أنتما.
items.qAr: في الإنجليزية ضمير خاص لمخاطبة شخصين مثل «أنتما».
items.why: English has only you. Add two or both: you two, you both.

items.q: 'How much are these sneakers?' asks about the price.
items.qAr: السؤال How much are these sneakers? يسأل عن السعر.

items.why: Say two pieces of furniture, or name the things: two chairs.

items.q: Groceries and leftovers are always plural.
items.qAr: كلمتا groceries و leftovers دائماً بصيغة الجمع.

missions.title: Picnic Planner
missions.intro: Listen, then record yourself planning the picnic.
missions.introAr: استمع ثم سجّل صوتك وأنت تخطّط للنزهة.
lines: How many bottles of juice do we need?
How much rice is there in the cupboard?
We don't need any bread. We have some leftovers.
Here's a piece of advice: always check your receipt!

missions.title: Kitchen Detective
missions.intro: Investigate your kitchen and teach your family!

steps.en: With permission, look in your kitchen and find 3 countable and 3 uncountable things.
steps.ar: بعد الاستئذان، ابحث في مطبخك عن 3 أشياء معدودة و3 أشياء غير معدودة.

steps.en: Teach someone at home the 'informations' trap: information, advice and homework have no -s.
steps.ar: علّم أحد أفراد أسرتك فخ «informations»: لا تُضاف -s إلى information و advice و homework.

steps.en: Ask a family member how many words for 'you' they know in other languages.
steps.ar: اسأل أحد أفراد أسرتك: كم كلمة لـ you يعرف في لغات أخرى؟
